Are you looking for a Tech job or an IT job?

For a Tech job - i.e. at a company that develops software as a product or as a service - what counts is your skills. What projects do you have on GitHub? Are there open-source projects that you contribute to? Can you sling code in an online interview? In my career, I have interviewed literally hundreds of candidates for such roles in my team - I am looking for guys with a solid grasp of CS principles who can apply what they learned in college and conceptualize a distributed queuing system on a whiteboard. This stuff is not easy - but that is what will get you past the hundreds of degree-holding wankers who have nothing else to show.

For an Software Development job - i.e. at a company where you develop applications or customize software for some business like a bank or whatever - they look for experience in that particular narrow software stack. A degree might be the minimum to open the door for an entry-level job.

For an IT job - i.e. you're basically making sure the computers work or the network stays up or the CI-system doesn't choke or the firewall stays secure - you need some credentials - usually certs - to show deep specialist expertise. For positions like this, I am looking for someone I can count on to keep things running. A "dev-ops" mindset, expertise in specific technologies, ability to automate the shit out of everything. You also need to be genuinely geeky about computers and how things work. (and personally, I wouldn't be able to do this job). A college degree is irrelevant.

A degree from most colleges is out of date by the time you graduate. Don't count on the degree alone to land you a job. You need to convince the interview panel that you actually learned something in the process, and can apply that creatively and with enough discipline to make it a viable product.

Don't let the gloomy comments about H1Bs get you down. Yes, at the bottom-tier you will run up against that, and it sucks. You need to start thinking about how you differentiate yourself. Show that you are a professional, have a strong sense of ownership, and can actually think and communicate intelligently. That you have that spark of creativity that can solve problems. That will elevate you above most applicants.

And sincerely, good luck in your career!
